title: US accuses Mexican judge of $2m bribe to free accused drug trafficker allegedly linked to ex-Olympic snowboarder
summary:
The judge oversaw extradition proceedings in Mexico for a Canadian citizen allegedly helping Ryan Wedding

A Mexican judge has been arrested and accused of accepting $2m in bribes in exchange…

blocks.text: A Mexican judge has been arrested and accused of accepting $2m in bribes in exchange for releasing a suspected Canadian drug trafficker from custody, US officials said on Thursday.

Luis Benítez Alcántara was overseeing extradition proceedings in Mexico in 2024 for Canadian citizen Andrew Clark, who was charged in the US with helping to run a billion-dollar drug-trafficking group allegedly headed by the former Canadian Olympic snowboarder Ryan Wedding, the justice department said in a statement.
Benítez is accused of releasing Clark from custody after accepting the bribe payments, according to the statement.
Clark was arrested days after his release and removed to the United States, where he faces drug-trafficking and murder charges.
The statement said Benítez, 49, was arrested on Sunday in Colombia. He is charged in a nine count indictment with being an accessory after the fact. It was not immediately known if he has a lawyer.
US officials will request Benítez’s extradition from Colombia, the statement said.

“Crooked public officials, no matter where they are, who assist drug traffickers operating here at home will face justice in the United States,” the US attorney general, Todd Blanche, said in the statement.

It is the latest arrest in the US investigation into a multinational drug-trafficking network allegedly run by Wedding, who became a top FBI fugitive accused of moving cocaine from Latin America into the United States and orchestrating several killings. Wedding was arrested in Mexico earlier this year and flown to California, where he pleaded not guilty to murder and drug charges.

Dozens of people have been arrested in connection with the alleged drug network, and authorities seized large volumes of drugs, weapons and cash, as well as millions of dollars’ worth of automobiles, motorcycles, artwork and jewelry in its investigation.
Clark’s attorney, Matthew Lombard, did not immediately respond to messages on Thursday.
